fields.title: South Korea Student Visa (D-2) from India: Fees and Steps
fields.summary: How to get a South Korea D-2 student visa from India: the USD 60 fee, the visa centre fee, documents, 14-working-day processing in New Delhi, part-time work and the job-seeking visa.
fields.seo_title: South Korea Student Visa from India: D-2 Fees & Steps
fields.meta_description: South Korea D-2 student visa for Indian students: USD 60 fee, ₹1,380 visa centre fee, documents, 14 working days in New Delhi and part-time work rules.
fields.body_md:
## The short answer

- **Visa:** a master's student needs a **D-2 visa**, in the D-2-3 sub-type for master's programmes. You apply at a Korean embassy or consulate general after your university sends its admission letter.
- **Where in India:** the Embassy in New Delhi, the Consulate General in Mumbai or the Consulate General in Chennai. Your passport's place of issue decides which one. You hand in papers at a visa application centre.
- **Fees:** the visa costs about **USD 60** (**₹5,575**) for a stay of 91 days or more. The New Delhi visa centre charges a service fee of **₹1,380**.
- **Money to show:** the Ministry of Justice standard is **KRW 20 million** (**₹13.89 lakh**) for capital-area universities. It is **KRW 16 million** (**₹11.11 lakh**) elsewhere. Read the details in our [proof of funds guide](/study-abroad/study-in/south-korea/south-korea-proof-of-funds-guide).
- **Time:** the New Delhi Embassy says **14 working days** for a normal application.
- **Stay:** up to **2 years** for each visa issue. Master's students can stay up to **5 years** in total with extensions.
- **After your degree:** you can change to a **D-10-1 job-seeking visa** for up to **2 years**.

Rupee amounts use **₹0.0694 per Korean won**. We built that rate from two official rates for 27 November 2026. One is the RBI rate of ₹92.91 per US dollar. The other is the Bank of Korea close of ₩1,337.9 per US dollar. Rates move every day. Your bank will charge its own rate, so treat the rupee figures as a guide.

## Before you apply

You cannot apply for a D-2 visa without an admission letter. Study in Korea says you prepare your documents "after receiving an admission letter". The letter is the **Standard Admission Letter** (also called a Certificate of Admission). Your university president or dean issues it.

Apply to universities first. See our [South Korea section](/study-abroad/study-in/south-korea) for universities and programmes.

## Which office handles your application

The Embassy page (in Korean) says a passport issued outside an office's area can be refused. Check the place of issue on your passport photo page. You can also check the city or state on the last page.

| Office | States and union territories |
|---|---|
| Embassy of Korea, New Delhi | Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Punjab, Sikkim, Tripura, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Delhi, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh |
| Consulate General, Mumbai | Goa, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu |
| Consulate General, Chennai | Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Lakshadweep |

The Embassy page covers New Delhi only. It says Mumbai and Chennai have different documents, methods and processing times. Check their own pages before you apply.

## Documents you need

Study in Korea lists these for a D-2 visa:

- **Passport:** a copy.
- **Photo:** one passport-size photo taken in the last 6 months.
- **Business registration certificate:** a copy of the university's certificate (or its registration number certificate).
- **Standard Admission Letter:** issued by the university president or dean.
- **Tuberculosis test result:** if it applies to you. Check the checklist for your office.
- **Proof of highest education:** your degree certificate.
- **Proof of financial ability:** see our [proof of funds guide](/study-abroad/study-in/south-korea/south-korea-proof-of-funds-guide).
- **Family relationship papers:** only if you use your parents' bank statements.

Study in Korea says extra documents may be needed, depending on your programme and your country. Each office has its own checklist for D-2 and D-4 visas.

The New Delhi Embassy has a separate checklist file for D-2 and D-4 visas. Its general guidance for Indians applying on an invitation lists income tax returns for the last 2 years. It also lists bank statements for 6 months. The Embassy says to treat that list as a reference only. It also says the officer may ask for other papers or an interview. Open the D-2 and D-4 checklist on the Embassy page before you collect your papers.

## Steps to apply

1. Get your admission letter from the university.
2. Check which office covers your passport.
3. Fill in the visa form online on the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr). Print it. The Embassy says to fill it in online, print it and hand it in at the visa centre.
4. Take your form and documents to the visa application centre. The Embassy does not take applications itself. The centres are open Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 13:00. The Kolkata centre opens at 10:00. The Embassy page lists centres in New Delhi and Kolkata only.
5. Pay the visa fee and the centre's service fee. The Embassy page does not say how the visa fee is paid.
6. Wait for the decision. Then travel to Korea.
7. Register as a foreign resident within **90 days** of entry.

## Fees

| Fee | Amount | In rupees |
|---|---|---|
| D-2 visa, stay of 91 days or more | **about USD 60** | ₹5,575 |
| Visa centre service fee, New Delhi and Kolkata (tax included) | **₹1,380** | ₹1,380 |

Study in Korea lists other visa fees too. A visit of 90 days or less costs about USD 40. A multiple-entry visa costs about USD 70 or USD 90. Those do not apply to a degree student.

Study in Korea calls the visa fee a processing fee for the application form. Ask the visa centre how to pay it before you go. The Embassy page names no service fee for Mumbai or Chennai.

## How long it takes

The New Delhi Embassy says a normal application takes **14 working days** from the application date. Applying at the Kolkata centre adds 2 to 3 days for courier. Urgent processing is suspended, so apply early. Extra document requests or checks add time.

The page gives no time for Mumbai or Chennai.

## Stay and extensions

A D-2 visa allows a stay of up to **2 years** for each issue. A master's student can stay up to **5 years** in total. The limit is 6 years for a 3-year programme. You apply for extensions in Korea.

After you arrive, register as a foreign resident within 90 days. Study in Korea lists the form, your passport, one photo and a fee. You also need a certificate of enrolment issued after entry.

## Work while you study

You need permission to work part time. Your university's international student adviser signs a part-time work form. You also need a standard work contract that states the hourly wage.

Study in Korea's table says master's and doctoral students can apply right away. Without a Korean-language certificate the limit is **15 hours** on weekdays and 15 hours at weekends and in vacations. With one it is **30 hours** on weekdays, with no limit at weekends and in vacations. The page lists 35 weekday hours at accredited universities with excellent academic and Korean-language results. It does not name the language standard for master's students. Ask your university.

Working without permission can bring penalties under the law.

## After your degree

Study in Korea says international students who finish their studies can change to a **D-10-1 job-seeking visa**. It can be extended in 6-month steps, up to **2 years**. Internships are allowed for up to 1 year within that time. Each company can host you for 6 months at most.

Your first change from D-2 to D-10 needs no proof of financial stability.

## Sources

Official pages, checked on 28 November 2026: [Study in Korea: Student Visa and Stay Status](https://www.studyinkorea.go.kr/en/plan/visaAndStay.do), [Embassy of Korea in India: visa guide for Indian applicants](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/in-ko/brd/m_2803/view.do?page=1&seq=1301843), [Study in Korea: Residence Eligibility and Stay Duration](https://www.studyinkorea.go.kr/en/life/residenceAndStayInfo.do) (registration, part-time work, job-seeking visa), [Korea Visa Portal](https://www.visa.go.kr), [Ministry of Justice press release, 5 February 2026](https://www.immigration.go.kr/bbs/moj/182/490464/download.do), [RBI exchange rates](https://www.rbi.org.in/) and the [Bank of Korea ECOS statistics](https://ecos.bok.or.kr).

faq_json.q: Which visa do I need to study a master's in South Korea?
faq_json.a: A D-2 visa. Master's programmes use the D-2-3 sub-type. You apply at a Korean embassy or consulate after your university sends its admission letter.

faq_json.q: How much is the South Korea student visa fee for Indian students?
faq_json.a: About USD 60 for a stay of 91 days or more, which is about ₹5,575. The New Delhi and Kolkata visa centre also charges a service fee of ₹1,380.

faq_json.q: Where do I apply for a Korean visa in India?
faq_json.a: At the Embassy in New Delhi, or the Consulate General in Mumbai or Chennai. The place of issue on your passport decides which one. You hand in papers at a visa application centre.

faq_json.q: How long does a Korean student visa take from India?
faq_json.a: The New Delhi Embassy says 14 working days for a normal application. Urgent processing is suspended. The Embassy page gives no time for Mumbai or Chennai. Extra document checks add time.

faq_json.q: Can I work part time on a D-2 visa?
faq_json.a: Yes, with permission. Study in Korea lists 15 hours for master's students without a Korean-language certificate, and 30 hours on weekdays with one. Weekend and vacation hours are unlimited with one.

faq_json.q: What happens after my master's degree in Korea?
faq_json.a: You can change to a D-10-1 job-seeking visa. It is extended in 6-month steps for up to 2 years.
